notes: The code is SUMMARIZED_CHILDHOOD and variedChildhood in src/simulation/character-history.ts. It is used for every grown character's earlier life in a new game (childhood-v3).

Placeholders in use now: a child who is five by September 1 starts kindergarten that fall. School years start between August 15 and September 8 and end between May 20 and June 15. 40% of childhoods include a move to another home in the same place. 50% of teenagers hold a part-time job at some point between 15 and 17 and a half, lasting 60 to 730 days. One to three remembered moments are drawn beyond one with a classmate and one with a teacher. The option taken in each moment is drawn uniformly.
The only teen job the game can write is 'Store assistant at Neighborhood Market'. This is the one employer every earlier version used, and it is kept as a marked placeholder.
Moments whose scene asserts a fact nothing recorded (a new sibling, an illness at home, a money shortfall) are left out of a summarized childhood on purpose, and remain playable.
Found in a playtest: two lives, in Rugby, North Dakota and Houma, Louisiana, had identical childhoods line for line, all dated on the birthday.

A140 (October 1, 2026): the school calendar no longer draws a start and end day for each child. Every child keeps one calendar: the school year starts on the first Monday on or after August 24 and ends on the Friday of its fortieth week (about 180 days of instruction and twenty of holidays and breaks), so classmates start and finish together. The rule is a PLACEHOLDER, the same in every district (src/simulation/school-stages.ts SCHOOL_STAGE_CALENDAR); part (3) of this question, the usual first and last days by state, would replace it, including states whose law sets the earliest start.
question: For a person growing up in the United States, and by state and birth year where it differs: (1) what share of children move home at least once before 18, and how often a move within the same town changes school; (2) the kindergarten age cutoff date by state; (3) the usual first and last days of the school year by state or region; (4) what share of teenagers hold a paid job before leaving high school, at what ages it starts, how long it lasts, and which jobs and kinds of employer are most common; and (5) whether some kinds of formative moment (owning up to breaking something, joining an activity, volunteering, organizing at school, falling out with a friend) are much more common than others.
requestedBy: The coordinator relaying a playtest finding, 2026-09-23 (about 9 p.m. Eastern): two different lives came out identical line for line. lamontae, 2026-09-22: 'a person's history is generated up to their age and the state of the world loaded into' and 'i dont want depth to be invented'.

title: How a summarized childhood varies: moves, school calendars, teen jobs and formative moments
usableAnswer: Shares and ranges per item, varying by state where they vary, as nationally sourced defaults with state overrides. For teen jobs: a short list of common job titles with the kind of employer for each. For formative moments: 'no defensible rate' is an acceptable answer, and the draw then stays uniform.
whyItMatters: Every grown character's earlier life is summarized when the game starts. Until this answer arrives, the shares and date windows that make two lives differ are marked stand-ins, and every teenager who works has the same job at the same store.
